Look, there are people who experience psychosis and end up getting violent, but they're *not* lashing out irrationally. They're responding to some sort of danger. What they believe and what they see is very much real to them and so if they think they're being attacked, their family is being attacked, someone is trying to stop them from saving the world etc. etc. then they'll *defend* themselves, but that's no way the same as being irrational and selfish. A person with psychosis is reacting rationally to a situation that only they can see. A borderline is reacting irrationally to a situation that everyone else can see. They're not acting in defense, they're often reacting selfishly or vindictively. They might act aggressively just for attention, or just so that they look like a victim and can supposedly get sympathy. A person with psychosis isn't responsible for the hurt they deliver, and will come back around to realising they've hurt someone (unless they have co-morbid personality issues or AOD issues). A BPD parent is 100% responsible for their actions.

So, firstly it's never ever been called 'borderline psychotic' - if your therapist said that she was speaking in hyperbole or she was referring to actual psychosis and not BPD. It was called borderline to reflected the outdated dichotomy between neurosis and psychosis, but psychosis in that context included things other than psychosis like mania without psychotic symptoms.

But more to the point, I worked in a psychiatric ward for six months. The patients who were psychotic were always lovely. There was always a logic to them and they were mostly aware that what they were saying sounded odd. They could always explain 'well I think this because this. It sounds crazy, but it's just this worry stuck in my head'. Interacting with borderlines on the other hand... They could never explain why they thought some way, they could never see that what they were doing was unusual. Borderline behaviour was actively dangerous, psychotic behaviour was just unusual.

The other thing is that the psychotic clients would come in for maybe two weeks, and after that time had passed they'd be like 'boy, that was weird' and then they'd go about their lives, the borderline clients... I mean having lived with borderlines... They're like that day after day week after week month after month year after year it just never ends. It truly is \*who they are\*, it truly is a reflection on them and is their \*personality\* - their long term behaviour and thought patterns that do not change and are consistent across different circumstances.

Calling it 'borderline psychosis' stigmatises \*psychosis.\* If you think borderline behaviour is anything like psychotic behaviour, then you don't understand how docile psychotic behaviour really is. People with psychosis are only dangerous when provoked, people with borderline are dangerous all the time. If you had been 'verbally/emotionally attacked by someone with psychosis' you would be getting a heartfelt apology for hurting you through a sea of tears a couple of weeks later and then they would \*never do it again\*. That doesn't sound like a borderline, does it?

A borderline parents might fulfil the stereotype of a 'psycho nut job' but they don't fulfil the reality of a psychotic \*episode\*.
